minutes.headline: Board deferred most special town meeting articles pending numbers, recommended others, and heard a staffing shortage report.
minutes.summary: The Select Board granted a one-day entertainment license, ratified two interim conservation administrators, and gave final recommendations on special town meeting warrant articles, keeping several deferred for lack of numbers. The town manager presented a detailed staffing-shortage report, and the board agreed pay is a central problem and asked for a workshop. The Municipal Building Design Committee reported on phasing and overlap with the school committee over Turkey Hill and TC Passios.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to recommend the opioid settlement stabilization transfer, Article Five, with one member saying he remained torn.
Articles one, two and three stay deferred pending final numbers, and the solar parking canopy article stays deferred because a height change was left out.
The board kept its earlier 3-1 recommendation on Article Six and recommended articles 7, 8, 10 through 14 and 16.
After the town manager's staffing-shortage report, the chair said a board workshop will be scheduled, with pay as the top item.
The board gave informal feedback, with no formal direction, to keep exploring overlap with the school committee on TC Passios and Turkey Hill.

why_it_matters: Special town meeting warrant articles that spend town money, including the opioid settlement transfer and the school climate-control transfer, are what residents will be asked to vote on, and several still lack final numbers.
Staffing shortages tied to pay can affect how well town services are staffed, and a pay workshop is the next step toward any change that would reach the budget.
watch_next: The board workshop on staffing, with pay as the top item, which the chair said will be scheduled.
Final numbers for articles one, two and three, and a revised solar parking canopy article, before the special town meeting.
